transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well... I'm not really sure how to explain it. I just... I keep having these strange moments. 

Like, I'll be sitting in my office, or even just at home, and... it just feels unreal. Like it's not actually happening. Sometimes it's almost like... like I'm watching myself from across the room, instead of actually being the one sitting there. It's just... unsettling, I guess.
Do you ever feel detached from your own body, as if you're watching yourself from outside, or as if you're not really in control of your own actions?

Yeah... that's pretty much what I just meant. The watching from outside part, anyway. I'll just be at my desk, and it feels like I'm seeing myself from the corner of the office. I don't really know about the control thing, but... yeah. It just feels unreal.
Do these feelings happen suddenly, like out of the blue, or do they usually come during times of stress or anxiety?
I don't really know. I haven't exactly kept track of it. It just... happens, I guess. I haven't really noticed if there's a pattern.
Have these feelings ever started after a particularly stressful or traumatic event, like an accident, a serious illness, or something scary that happened to you?

...I suppose so. It's been going on for about two weeks now. I had a... a situation at work. A client got pretty upset and... well, he threatened me. Right in my office. So... yeah. It's been happening since then.
Have you noticed if these feelings of unreality or watching yourself happen often, or do they just come every once in a while?
I don't really know. Just... every once in a while, I guess. I try not to dwell on it too much when it's not happening.
Have you ever felt confused about who you are, or felt like you're changing into a different person at times?
No, not really. I mean, I know who I am. I'm just... trying to get through the day. I haven't felt like a different person or anything like that.
Do these feelings of watching yourself or feeling detached happen frequently enough that they interfere with your daily life, or are they just occasional and mild?

I suppose... it's affecting things. I've, uh... I've missed a few client deadlines lately. I actually stopped seeing people at the office entirely. I just... I don't really trust myself to handle the returns right now. Or to keep the workplace safe, really. So... yeah. It interferes.
Do you ever feel like the world around you seems unreal or like you're in a dream, even when you're fully awake?
No... not exactly like a dream. It's just... I'm just tired, I think. I haven't really noticed the world looking unreal. Just... everything feels a bit distant. But not a dream.
Do you feel like these episodes of watching yourself are happening more often now compared to when they first started, or do they still happen only once in a while?
I'm not... I don't really know. I haven't exactly been keeping track of it. It just... happens sometimes. I couldn't tell you if it's more often or not.
How long do these episodes of feeling detached or watching yourself usually last when they happen?
I'm not really sure. I don't... I don't time them. It's just a feeling that comes and goes. I couldn't give you an exact number of minutes or anything.
When you feel like you're watching yourself, do you also feel a sense of being detached from your body or emotions, as if you're not fully connected to yourself?

I guess so. It's... it's hard to explain. When it happens, it's like I'm not really there. Like I'm... watching myself from across the room. Especially at home, or... or when I'm at the office. It just feels... unreal. Like I'm disconnected from it all.
When you feel like you're watching yourself, does the world around you also seem strange or unreal, like it's not quite real, or does it just feel like you're disconnected from yourself?

I suppose it's both. Like I was saying... my own house just feels unreal. The office, too. It's not just me feeling disconnected, the places themselves seem... strange. Like I'm not actually there in the room.
When you feel this sense of watching yourself or being detached, do you ever lose touch with reality or have trouble telling what’s real and what isn’t?
No, I... I don't think so. I know what's real. It's just... a feeling. I'm not losing my mind or anything.
Do these feelings of watching yourself or feeling detached ever go away completely, or do they seem to be constantly present in the background even when they're not intense?
I'm not really sure. I guess they go away. I... I haven't really paid attention to whether it's always there in the background. I just notice it when it happens.
Are there times when you don’t feel any of this detachment or unreality, where everything feels completely normal, or does it always feel somewhat off in the background?
Like I said, I... I don't really keep track of it like that. I suppose there are normal times. I'm just trying to get my work done, really. I haven't sat down and analyzed it.
Do these feelings of watching yourself or feeling detached ever completely go away for periods of time, or do you feel like they are always somewhere in the background, even if mild?
Doctor, you... you just asked me that. Like I said, I don't know if it's always there in the background. I just... I try to focus on my work. I haven't really thought about it that deeply.

Are there times when you feel completely free of these experiences—when everything feels totally real and connected—or does there always seem to be some degree of detachment or unreality, even if it's mild?
I... I really don't know how else to answer this. We just went over this. I'm... I'm not keeping a log of when things feel real or not. I'm just trying to get through the day and do my job.
